results.answer: Controlled lowering and full depth are key — focus on feeling your quads working, not your lower back. results.answer: For your chest, focus on heavy weights with low reps, keeping your shoulder blades set and maintaining a steady bar path. results.question: how should I train my quads with my knee?
results.answer: Train your quads with controlled movements, focusing on the thighs rather than the lower back. Keep the weight on your legs and avoid overloading the knees. Stick to a range that feels comfortable for your knee, and stop if you feel any sharp pain. For more details, check the Workout screen in the app.

results.question: how should I warm up for tendonitis?
results.answer: For tendonitis, warm up your joints properly before any heavy sets, and build the load gradually—tendons adapt more slowly than muscles. Isometric holds under load can also help build tendon strength. Make sure to take it easy and avoid jumping the weight just because the muscle feels ready. If it persists, a physio or doctor might be able to help.

results.question: what should I do for my tendons when I lift my shoulders?
results.answer: For your tendons when lifting your shoulders, warm up the joint thoroughly and build the load gradually. Hold positions still at a pain-free angle, and avoid heavy overhead or pressing work if it causes sharp pain. Focus on lighter, controlled movements and let your tendons strengthen over time.
